item.title: Chicago's Broadview Six Case Shows How the DOJ Is Losing Public Trust
item.description: When government lawyers appear in federal court, they enjoy something called “the presumption of regularity,” which is a fancy way of saying that judges give them the benefit of the doubt. President Donald Trump’s administration is now in danger of squandering this trust — to the detriment of not only federal prosecutors, but also public safety.
item.dc:creator: Barbara McQuade

item.title: The Real Message of the Midterms? Know Thy Enemy
item.description: Two years into President Donald Trump’s second term, the country told him loud and clear it’s had enough. Will this “Watergate-level repudiation,” as Republican Senator Ted Cruz called it, summon repairs to America’s fractured politics? In a word, no.
item.dc:creator: Clive Crook

item.title: Skydance’s DC Studios Shakeup Could Release It From Superhero Slump
item.description: You know what might be really super for the media giant? Making movies that can stand on their own merits.
item.dc:creator: Brooke Sample

item.title: Poland Is a Warning for Vengeful US Democrats
item.description: Poles, shocked by a mass shooting in the heart of the historic city of Krakow, might have been comforted that their fractious political class was at least willing to mourn together. In the aftermath, the right-wing President Karol Nawrocki and the liberal pro-European Prime Minister Donald Tusk laid down candles together in the town’s main market square.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Microsoft Outlook Outage Is a Bad Look for a AI Layoffs
item.description: We’ve all been there: Your WiFi is down and you need a human to fix it, but first you have to run the gauntlet of the cable company’s dimwitted AI robots to access one. Now imagine you’re a $4 trillion company and the entire planet needs your computer problems fixed, like, yesterday, but you’ve sacrificed a third of your human employees to AI.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff
